<reason>A establishes a persuasive case against redundant GMO burdens, but B better contests the proposed editing-specific distinction. B explains how published risk-based criteria remove unnecessary requirements upfront while retaining targeted testing, directly answering both cost and conventional-breeding pressure. A repeatedly attributes full dossiers and litigated waivers to an alternative requiring neither, and prematurely alleges nonresponse before B’s scheduled answer. The competing designs converge substantially, limiting the winning margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal dismantles A’s “toll booth” comparison: relief need not require either a preliminary full dossier or litigation. B also identifies a concrete comparative disadvantage in A’s design—escalating plausible concerns into full review where B would require only targeted testing.</best_rebuttal>
